drivingQuestion: What does Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya's a fortiori add beyond the ruling of the first tanna?
outcomeNote: The unit ends with the difficulty standing; it is answered in the following unit by the difference over Rabbi Ila's Usha ordinance.

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה: אִם לַגָּבוֹהַּ אֵין אָדָם רַשַּׁאי כּוּ׳. הַיְינוּ תַּנָּא קַמָּא!
segments.en: § The mishna teaches that «Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya said: If for the Most High a person» may «not» dedicate all his property, it is all the more so the case that one should spare his property and not give it all to others. The Gemara raises a difficulty: «This is» identical to the opinion of «the first tanna,» i.e., Rabbi Eliezer, who prohibits the dedication of all one’s property.
